title: Money — Meaning, Functions, Evolution & Types

content.text: Indian Economy — Money & Banking basics (barter → coins → digital money).
Q — What was the Barter system and why did it fail?
Barter = direct exchange of goods for goods (introduced by Mesopotamian tribes). It broke down because of:
— both sides must want exactly what the other offers.
— finding the right counterparty is costly.
— perishable goods lose value; hard to store.
Layman: if you grow tomatoes and want shoes, you must find a shoemaker who also wants tomatoes — clumsy. So a common 'middle good' (money) was invented.
Q — What are the functions of money?
Measure of value; Medium of exchange
Store of value; Transfer of value; Standard of deferred payments (EMI)
Basis of financial market; Mobilises factors of production; Helps redistribution of national income
Layman: money is a ruler (measures worth), a token (buy/sell now), a piggy-bank (save), and a promise (pay later via EMI).
Q — How did money evolve, and what are its types?
Commodity Money → Metallic Money → Paper / Token / Fiat Money → Bank (Deposit) Money → Cryptocurrency.

Value comes from govt command ('fiat'); it is legal tender.
Prone to Debasement (↓ metal content when a ruler is weak/poor — e.g., Aurangzeb, Roman kings)

Syllabus (GS3): Indian Economy — Money & Banking basics (barter → coins → digital money).

Q — What was the Barter system and why did it fail?

Concept: Barter = direct exchange of goods for goods (introduced by Mesopotamian tribes). It broke down because of:





Double coincidence of wants — both sides must want exactly what the other offers.



High search & transaction cost — finding the right counterparty is costly.



Poor store of value — perishable goods lose value; hard to store.



No specialization — discourages division of labour.

Layman: if you grow tomatoes and want shoes, you must find a shoemaker who also wants tomatoes — clumsy. So a common 'middle good' (money) was invented.

Q — What are the functions of money?







Category



Functions





Primary



Measure of value; Medium of exchange





Secondary



Store of value; Transfer of value; Standard of deferred payments (EMI)





Contingent



Basis of financial market; Mobilises factors of production; Helps redistribution of national income

Layman: money is a ruler (measures worth), a token (buy/sell now), a piggy-bank (save), and a promise (pay later via EMI).

Q — How did money evolve, and what are its types?

Evolution: Commodity Money → Metallic Money → Paper / Token / Fiat Money → Bank (Deposit) Money → Cryptocurrency.







Type



Intrinsic value?



Key points & examples





Commodity money



Yes



Iron nails, bear pelts, cocoa beans, whale teeth, gold nuggets. Problems: perishable, not uniform, not pure, foreigners may reject.





Metallic money



Yes



Kings stamped gold for trust. Indo-Greek & Kushana gold coins; Gupta coins most spectacular. Delhi Sultanate: Silver Tanka; Sher Shah Suri: Rupiya; Akbar: Muhr.





Paper / Fiat money



No



Value comes from govt command ('fiat'); it is legal tender.





Bank / Deposit money



No



Cheque, Demand Draft, digital transfers.





Cryptocurrency



No



Decentralised, blockchain-based.

Q — Full-bodied vs Token coins?







Basis



Full-bodied coins



Token coins





Example



Gupta coin (~8 gm gold)



50 paisa modern coin (~4 gm steel)





Intrinsic vs face value



Intrinsic value ≥ face value



Intrinsic value < face value





Key point



Prone to Debasement (↓ metal content when a ruler is weak/poor — e.g., Aurangzeb, Roman kings)



Modern Indian coins are token coins; cupronickel discourages melting; Coinage Act 2011 bans melting coins

Key facts / GK





1330s: Tughlaq's token-coin experiment failed (#EpicFail).



Coinage Act, 2011 — melting/destroying coins is an offence.



USA (2025): stopped minting the penny — a 1-cent penny cost ~4 cents to make.
